entries.title: While the Bears rested, the NFC North proved nasty
entries.summary: <p>A week ago, Ben Johnson looked at the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ bye week as a challenge — a time for the coach to figure out how to improve everything from run-game explosiveness to quarterback consistency to defensive oomph.</p><p>“There's a great opportunity at hand just to look at these first nine games and come away with what we're doing well and what we can lean on going into the last stretch of the season,” he said. “And certainly some areas of improvement that we need to get better at.”</p><p>What went unspoken was exactly why the Bears needed to be so sharp. Despite going 7-2 in their first nine games, they were far from the runaway favorite to win the NFC North. The Bears’ division is the best in the NFL, and by the end of the season could be considered one of the best in league history. If the Bears played in the NFC South, they’d be in first place by three games. In the NFC North, they’re in third place.</p><p>How nasty is the NFC North? The Bears didn’t play a game Sunday and fell four spots in the NFC’s playoff picture. Even with the Lions likely losing star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a knee injury, the division is a gauntlet. The Vikings’ dominance of the Packers at Lambeau Field reinforced as much.</p><p>Johnson is chasing perfection out of necessity. Without it, the Bears could miss the postseason. They are one of three NFC North teams sitting at 7-2 after Sunday, with the Packers at 6-4.</p><p>“There's a certain standard that we want to hit week-in and week-out,” he said. “I think the good teams, even when they get victories, if they don't hit those benchmarks then that leaves some more to be desired. And I felt that from our crew, which is a good thing.</p><p>“I think that's the next evolution of this team, not just that we win but the manner in which we play."</p><p>After they beat the Seahawks, the Bears spent a week being <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/12/catch-22-bears-cris-collinsworth-mike-tomlin-built-go-far-caleb-williams-ben-johnson-bye-week" >touted by national talking heads </a>as a Super Bowl favorite. A week later, while the Bears were busy winning ugly against the Buccaneers, the Packers inherited that mantle when they thumped the defending AFC champion Patriots in New England.</p><p>This week, it will be the Vikings, who emerged as the league’s big winner of the weekend by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/vikings-beat-packers-30-10-in-kirk-cousins-return-jordan-love-is-sacked-8-times" >dispatching the Packers 30-10</a> at Lambeau Field. The Bears, by contrast, lost 31-7 in the same place a month ago.</p><p>Quarterback Kirk Cousins steadied the ship Sunday, five days after being traded by the Raiders and six days after Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz looked lost in a “Monday Night Football” debacle against the Bills. The Vikings’ defense continued to do what it’s done all season — perform like the best single unit on either side of the ball in the NFL.</p><p>The Vikings tortured Jordan Love, sacking the Packers quarterback eight times. They forced four turnovers — one interception and a whopping three fumbles. The last time the Vikings had eight sacks and four takeaways in one game was 37 years ago.</p><p>That blitzing formula worked for the Vikings against the Bears in Week 2 — and for the Buccaneers a week ago. While NFL teams figure to blitz Bears quarterback Caleb Williams even more going forward, no one does it as well as Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores.</p><p>Cousins was solid Sunday, throwing for 207 yards and two touchdowns. More importantly, star receiver Justin Jefferson looked far more comfortable with Cousins that he did Wentz or Kyler Murray. His 13 targets were the most he’s had all season, while his 74 receiving yards were his most in five weeks.</p><p>The Vikings, though, don’t even sit in first place in the North anymore. The Lions do — but their long flight home from Germany after a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/lions-patriots-munich-drake-maye-aiden-hutchinson-injuries" >35-10 win against the Patriots </a>was undoubtedly muted.</p><p>Hutchinson hurt his knee while celebrating a sack of the Patriots’ Drake Maye, who was subsequently knocked out of the game. The Lions planned for him to get further examinations when they landed back in America but reportedly fear that he’ll be lost for the season. It was reminiscent of former Bears linebacker Lamarr Houston tearing his ACL while celebrating a sack of the Patriots’ backup quarterback in a 2014 game in which the Bears were trailing by 25 points.</p><p>The timing is notable for the Lions — and the Bears. Losing Hutchinson just days after the NFL’s trade deadline would leave a gaping hole in a Lions defense that was suspect to begin with. Without him, their defense isn’t Super Bowl quality.</p><p>The Bears could take advantage soon, too — the Lions play the Buccaneers next week before hosting the Bears on Thanksgiving Day. Johnson has never beaten his former team. The Bears need a divisional win desperately, having lost to both the Packers and Vikings earlier this season.</p><p>The Thanksgiving game starts a run of four divisional games over the Bears’ final seven contests. Every game, every detail has a chance to tilt the division.</p><p>The Bears learned that Sunday without even taking the field.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/vikings-beat-packers-30-10-in-kirk-cousins-return-jordan-love-is-sacked-8-times" >Vikings beat Packers 30-10 in Kirk Cousins’ return; Jordan Love is sacked 8 times</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/lions-patriots-munich-drake-maye-aiden-hutchinson-injuries" >Lions rout Patriots 35-10 in Munich; Aidan Hutchinson reportedly out for the season</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/11/15/bears-next-opponent-saints-fall-to-the-panthers-20-17" >Bears’ next opponent: Saints fall to the Panthers 20-17</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Lions rout Patriots 35-10 in Munich; Aidan Hutchinson reportedly out for the season
entries.summary: <p>MUNICH — Amon-Ra St. Brown wore lederhosen, carried a German flag onto the field, and then went out and scored two touchdowns.</p><p>Talk about a homecoming.</p><p>The German-speaking St. Brown, whose mother is from Leverkusen, said it's been a trip he'll "never forget."</p><p>St. Brown caught two touchdown passes and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two scores in a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots, who lost quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury on their opening drive Sunday.</p><p>"Being in Germany, number one, was a blessing, it's been amazing," St. Brown said. "But being able to win like that — with the guys, my teammates in front of the fans here in Germany, it's like a dream come true."</p><p>The Lions (7-2) have won five straight games but also lost edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who hurt his right knee while celebrating the sack that knocked Maye out of the game. A person familiar with the situation later told The Associated Press that Hutchinson's injury was season-ending.</p><p>"Any time you lose a player like that and you don't know the entirety of it ... it hurts a little bit," Lions coach Dan Campbell said.</p><p>Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, along with two interceptions, completing 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards.</p><p>St. Brown caught a 56-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter to give Detroit a 7-3 lead. And his 28-yard TD reception — after teammates pushed him over the goal line in a scrum with Patriots defenders — made it 28-3 in the third quarter.</p><p>St. Brown, who wore lederhosen for his arrival to the stadium, charged onto the field carrying a German flag. St. Brown and his two brothers spent many summers in their childhood visiting the country.</p><p>In between St. Brown's scores, Goff found Isaac TeSlaa for a 12-yard touchdown pass and a 14-3 lead after a 97-yard drive, and Gibbs ran it in from 5 yards one play after he rumbled down the sideline for a 50-yard reception.</p><p>Gibbs added a 28-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to make it 35-10. He is the first NFL player since Priest Holmes in 2002 to produce more than 150 yards rushing with two rushing touchdowns and at least 95 yards receiving in a game, the Lions said.</p><p>Gibbs caught seven passes for 99 yards. St. Brown finished with four receptions for 98 yards.</p><p>The Patriots (5-5) have lost back-to-back games and three of four.</p><p>Tommy DeVito completed 12 of 24 for 81 yards with one interception and a fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Lan Larison for New England.</p><p>On his only drive, Maye completed three of four passes for 48 yards. He also scrambled for 11 yards. Hutchinson sacked Maye at the Detroit 15-yard line on third down. Andy Borregales then kicked a 33-yard field goal.</p><p>New England coach Mike Vrabel he didn't know the extent of Maye's injury: "We'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has."</p><p>After DeVito entered the game, the Patriots punted on four straight possessions. DeVito then threw an interception to Roger McCreary late in the first half. The Lions couldn't capitalize, though. Goff was picked off in the back of the end zone by Kevin Byard III.</p><p>Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez had his first interception of the season in the first half. Mack Hollins led the Patriots with five catches for 48 yards.</p><p>"We're heading into the bye and we have to get some things fixed and changed and corrected and figure out ways to win as opposed to what we're doing right now, which is not giving ourselves enough of a chance," Vrabel said.</p><h3>New field incoming</h3><h3></h3><p>Immediately after the game, workers will start installing a new field. Bayern Munich hosts Cologne on Friday night in a Bundesliga game. The NFL wouldn't confirm a German media report that said the league would pay up to 200,000 euros ($220,000) for the new pitch. In a statement to AP, the league said only that it will "work in partnership with Allianz Arena to replace the field following Sunday's game."</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Patriots:</b> Besides Maye, WR A.J. Brown left in the second half with a hamstring injury. Brown had missed the past two games with ankle and knee problems... RT Morgan Moses left in the first quarter but returned before halftime ... RB TreVeyon Henderson, who didn't make the trip, was placed on injured reserve Saturday.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Patriots:</b> Bye week.</p><p><b>Lions:</b> Host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: Workers at 3 more hotels join strike for better wages, benefits
entries.summary: <p>Hundreds of hospitality workers at three prominent Chicago hotels have joined an ongoing strike for better wages and benefits, the workers' union announced Sunday.</p><p>Workers at the Marriott Marquis, Royal Sonesta and The Wade Hotel, represented by the union UNITE HERE Local 1, walked off the job Sunday. Hundreds of others at the Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk, Waldorf Astoria Chicago, Palmer House a Hilton Hotel, The Westin Chicago River North, Westin Michigan Avenue, Millennium Hotel Knickerbocker, Hilton Chicago and Hyatt Regency Chicago have been on strike already this fall, many of them since mid-October when strikes at six hotels began ahead of the Chicago Marathon.</p><p>Workers say they are overworked and not paid fairly, and they're hoping a strike prompts progress at the bargaining table.</p><p>“I don’t want to be on strike, especially with this cold weather," said Maria Jimenez, a housekeeper at the Royal Sonesta. “But this is what we have to do. We the workers keep the hotels running, and yet it isn’t enough for these companies. They’re not respecting us at the negotiating table."</p><p>Hotel employees are strapped financially, according to the union, with around one-third of members reporting they struggle to cover rent and utilities, according to a 2025 survey conducted by the union. Contracts with Hyatt, Marriott and Hilton expired Aug. 31.</p><p>Royal Sonesta and Marriott, which operates Marriott Marquis and The Wade Hotel, didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Holiday desserts for grown-ups spark controversy
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My family gathers for holidays like so many. I love making different treats, including desserts or fruit soaked in brandy. Everyone loves them, and they're kept well out of children's reach. One person is objecting to this and asking that I not bring it. They say their kids are asking why they can't have the brandied fruit, and they're uncomfortable explaining. They feel nothing should be off-limits.</p><p>I don't understand this. When I was growing up, there was always adult punch and other things we kids couldn't have. I feel the explanation is simple: Some things are for grown-ups. The hosts are afraid of causing a rift. Should we go along and let the kids be in charge, or should this be a teaching moment? — <i>ADULTS ONLY</i></p><p><b>DEAR ADULTS ONLY:</b> The simplest solution would be to make a nonalcoholic version of your dish and serve that to any minors — or abstaining adults — who express an interest. (For the record, if this parent is uncomfortable explaining the rules of modern society to their kids, I think you'd be an excellent candidate for the job.)</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I have been happily married for 32 years. Unfortunately, my wife's two sisters and her mother have rejected me. Two of the three have said so. I don't believe I have done anything wrong and have asked them why, which they refuse to reveal. They are nasty to me and falsely accuse me of being a "controlling husband" who does not let my wife go out with girlfriends. They ask my wife to choose between me and them, and they weaponize my son's hospitalization by intentionally not showing any caring.</p><p>Eight years ago, at the age of 52, I was formally diagnosed by my therapist as having autism. The in-laws said, "Had we known you were autistic, things would have been different." This was painful for me, as I don't believe in wearing medical issues or disabilities as a badge, and I think it elicits prejudice.</p><p>I believe (but cannot prove) that the reason they have rejected me is because I am not of their ethnicity, I have an introverted personality and am on the autism spectrum, or some combination. I have concluded this because my ex-brother-in-law was treated similarly. He chose a divorce and another partner with whom to move forward. I am not interested in that solution, but I am miserable.</p><p>My wife and son agree with my assessment and are supportive, but I can't find a way to move forward. Can you help? — <i>MISERABLE IN PENNSYLVANIA</i></p><p><b>DEAR MISERABLE:</b> I can try. Rather than make yourself miserable because your wife's family refuses to accept you, quit trying. A way to move forward that has worked for many other people is to start forming a "chosen" family and expose yourself as little as possible to your in-laws. A chosen family is comprised of people who like and respect you and your wife, and whose company you can enjoy without feeling judged. You may be introverted, but you do not have to be isolated.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: Public health advocates call for stricter nitrate standards in drinking water
entries.summary: <p>A coalition of environmental and public health organizations are calling on federal regulators to revise the nationwide limit on toxic nitrates allowed in drinking water.</p><p>National and local advocacy groups like the Natural Resources Defense Council, Food & Water Watch, Prairie Rivers Network, and 11 others warn in the <a class="Link" href="https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28896368-epa-nitrate-petition/" target="_blank" >petition</a> submitted Monday to the U.S Environmental Protection Agency that “nitrates in drinking water are causing a public health crisis across the country.”</p><p>Nitrate is a key chemical compound common in fertilizer, which can contaminate drinking water sources. Recent studies have linked nitrate in drinking water with colorectal cancer, thyroid disease, and fetal abnormalities.</p><p>Illinois is a hot spot for nitrate pollution. Agricultural runoff can seep into groundwater and flow into streams, rivers, and reservoirs.</p><p>“One in three Americans are currently being served water with dangerous levels of nitrate in it,” said Tyler Lobdell, a senior staff attorney at Food & Water Watch.</p><p>The coalition is requesting the US EPA change the maximum contaminant level of nitrate in drinking water standard from 10 mg/L to 1 mg/liter.</p><p>“This change would reflect the best available, peer- reviewed science and would bring substantial health benefits to communities across the country,” according to the petition.</p><p>Between 2021, and 2023, more than 2 million people in Illinois were served drinking water that tested above 1 milligram of nitrate per liter, according to Robert Hirschfeld, the director of water policy at the Illinois environmental group Prairie Rivers Network.</p><p>“I would like to see this petition put the state of Illinois on notice that nitrate is a significant problem,” Hirschfeld said.</p><p>Opponents of the current federal drinking water standard for nitrate — set today at a limit of 10 milligrams per liter — worry that the decades-old benchmark is out of date.</p><p>The longstanding threshold was set as a placeholder in 1975 and formally adopted in 1991 based on the risk of blue baby syndrome, a condition in which newborns exhibit discoloration due to low levels of oxygen.</p><p>A growing body of research is pointing to additional health issues bearing down on rural America where industrial agriculture is most prevalent. Now, advocates want public health officials to adopt tougher safety standards for drinking water.</p><p>EPA has tried to reassess the nitrate benchmark twice, first under the Obama administration and then again under the Biden administration. The first and second Trump administrations scuttled both efforts.</p><p>“We've done the EPA's work for it," Lobdell said.</p><p>As part of its petition, the coalition compiled the latest science and a 43-page cost-benefit analysis to justify the stricter limit.</p><p>The petitions ask the EPA to take two immediate steps. First, the agency should institute an interim protective threshold for nitrate while they adopt a new limit. Second, they should enforce other federal protections like the Clean Water Act and rein in industrial agriculture, which Lobdell said has been given a “free pass to pollute.”</p>

entries.title: CPS overtime pay costs skyrocketed despite a 2022 warning to rein in spending
entries.summary: <p>Extra pay earned by Chicago Public Schools staff exploded in recent years after the district failed to heed some recommendations issued in 2022 that might have brought the spending under control.</p><p>That’s according to a new report from the CPS inspector general’s office, released Monday. The inspector general found the school district’s overtime costs tripled from 2019 to a peak of $150 million in 2024. In 2025, the most recent year examined by the OIG, the amount dropped to $97 million.</p><p>“When it goes unmonitored and untracked, it can absolutely lead to fraud and waste, we've seen it in our investigations over the years,” Inspector General Philip Wagenknecht said. “We’ve had cases where clerks are involved in paying themselves over time. Several years ago, we had a principal who was indicted and convicted for a phony extra pay scheme where she was distributing the pay to her staff and requiring them to kick it back to her.”</p><p>Wagenknecht’s office found issues with extra pay to employees among a range of positions and parts of CPS but found particularly high levels among custodians. One custodian, for example, punched in and out of work for 77 days in a row, including weekends.</p><p>CPS officials say they take the Inspector General’s findings “seriously and are continuing to strengthen controls over extra pay, including overtime, extended day and stipends. The District will continue to review and update guidance and monitor payroll procedures.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-100000" name="html-embed-module-100000"></a><div style="min-height:540px" id="datawrapper-vis-1qN4z"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/1qN4z/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-1qN4z"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/1qN4z/full.png" alt="Spending on extra pay at CPS has increased dramatically since 2019 (Column Chart)" /></noscript></div> </div> </div><p>The report comes as the school district has had to cut to close budget deficits for the past three years and is expected to face one again this coming year.</p><p>The inspector general’s report is a follow-up to one in 2022 that pointed out the district lacked controls on extra pay and expressed concern that “spending might continue to rise unchecked, especially with federal COVID relief funding available.” CPS received $2.8 billion in COVID-19 relief funds, which it had to spend by the end of 2025.</p><p>“Unfortunately, the OIG’s prediction came true,” the inspector general wrote in the report, referring to the Office of the Inspector General.</p><p>In response to the report, CPS officials say they have or are working on implementing some of the recommendations. These include capping what employees can earn in a given period through what’s known as “extended day pay” and creating a system to monitor whether protocols are being followed.</p><p>The OIG examined different types of extra pay: traditional overtime for hourly workers, typically 1.5 times their rate; and extended day pay, which is paid by the hour; and lump-sum stipends, which are two categories of pay teachers and other staff can earn for work done outside their standard schedule, like running a club or a sport.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-d50000" name="html-embed-module-d50000"></a><div style="min-height:538px" id="datawrapper-vis-SUro7"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/SUro7/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-SUro7"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/SUro7/full.png" alt="How CPS doled out extra pay in the 2025 fiscal year (Pie Chart)" /></noscript></div> </div> </div><p>CPS put aside more than $100 million in COVID-relief money for extended day payments as the district sought to recoup learning loss and increase attendance through after-school programs.</p><p>Yet the inspector general noted, back in 2022, the deployment of those extra pay dollars was ripe for fraud and CPS did not have limits, accepted paperwork without proper approvals and did not monitor it to catch excessive payments.</p><p>And the inspector general’s new report details a number of situations where employees appeared to collect a lot of extra pay without questions. For example, over four years, six employees made $200,000 in extra pay and 147 made $100,000 in extra pay.</p><p>The facilities department and its custodians received the most overtime pay in each of the years the inspector general reviewed. His office noted the costs in 2025 might be a result of the district laying off 160 custodians who clean schools. CPS kept all the 1,225 custodians employed by the district. This resulted in a 6% drop in custodian positions.</p><p>Even if there was more work to do, some of the extra pay for custodians was exorbitant, the report said. One custodian took home $275,000 in extra pay over four years. Another earned $81,000, in addition to a regular salary of $61,000, in 2025.</p><p>CPS noted in 2025 the management of custodians was in transition as the district took it over after it had been privatized for more than a decade.</p>

" srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/15e8e48/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+101/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa2%2Fae%2Fba2046f6488facdea01c17208270%2Fspectrum-261115-8.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/2287b64/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+101/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa2%2Fae%2Fba2046f6488facdea01c17208270%2Fspectrum-261115-8.png 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/15e8e48/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+101/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa2%2Fae%2Fba2046f6488facdea01c17208270%2Fspectrum-261115-8.png" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>“I think it’s how Jaime and I both show up in our music-making — we’re here to have fun and play good music, and share it with you, and have a good time,” Cleo Goldberg shared. </p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Mark Black for the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Goldberg, who also uses they/them pronouns, will perform in Spectrum’s debut as a Chicago-based ensemble Nov. 17 at The CheckOut. “I think it’s how Jaime and I both show up in our music-making — we’re here to have fun and play good music, and share it with you, and have a good time.”</p><p>For example, in the inaugural concert, the program includes a marimba-vibraphone arrangement of “Maria” from “West Side Story”; a dead-serious patty-cake game called “Kid Gunner Brother”; and a piece by former Chicagoan Alex Temple called “Ah yes, the three genders,” in reference to an internet meme. Here, instead of referring to found alignments of three items such as printed guides prominently labeled “girl,” “boy” and “mischief,” the title refers to the percussion-instrument classifications of wood, metal and skins.</p><p>A piece called “Golden Gate,” a vibraphone-marimba duet that manages to sound both insistent and meditative, has a memorable origin. The composer, Kevin Rosacia, wrote it as an ode to what the city of San Francisco has meant to gay culture and about building a bridge to connect himself with the LGBTQ community. Spectrum plays only the music of queer composers. When the ensemble put out a call for commissions, Rosacia responded, even though he wasn’t yet out.</p><p>“So he used this as his coming-out piece,” Esposito said, “which was pretty inspiring and special for us to be able to do.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-a50000" name="image-a50000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/280e327/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e0541db/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b0fe72d/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Jaime Esposito of Spectrum Ensemble performs during the Going Dutch Festival at Side Street Studio Arts in Elgin on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b0fe72d/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/7ef686c/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b0fe72d/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F6c%2F3a%2Fb31d34e549cfa2894d59cd073c65%2Fspectrum-261115-10.png" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>“Like the concert black, we don’t play that game,” Esposito said. “We wear jumpsuits with rainbows and our names on the back, because it doesn’t need to be that serious.”</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Mark Black for the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The ensemble also is staging a suite called “Dorothy Fragments,” a theatrical piece where some fragments are played, some are spoken, and one includes clacking folding fans. The title is a reference to the shibboleth “friend of Dorothy,” which gay people used to identify one another in the mid-20th century. Another Dorothy fragment calls for a death drop, a dance move from drag culture where the dancer falls suddenly to a supine position with one leg folded underneath. “Luckily, that’s Cleo’s part,” Esposito said. (Elsewhere in their performance life, Goldberg performs as the drag queen Manic Maxxie.)</p><p>Clearly, the normal protocols of classical-tradition concertgoing are out the window. “Like the concert black, we don’t play that game,” Esposito said. “We wear jumpsuits with rainbows and our names on the back, because it doesn’t need to be that serious.”</p><p>Goldberg’s first appearance with Spectrum came during the COVID-19 pandemic, when Manic Maxxie cameoed in full glam to do the death drop routine in an online performance of “Dorothy Fragments.” Goldberg and Esposito knew each other from percussion symposia and past festivals, dating to when Goldberg was in high school and Esposito attended Northwestern. So when Esposito moved back to Chicago in January for a day-job opportunity, they invited Goldberg to team up to re-establish the duo.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-700000" name="image-700000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1dd671b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a49dfd4/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a80fd45/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Spectrum Ensemble consisting of Jaime Esposito and Cleo Goldberg perform during the Going Dutch Festival at Side Street Studio Arts in Elgin on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a80fd45/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b4643a6/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a80fd45/2147483647/strip/true/crop/2500x1403+0+132/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F66%2F77%2Fdd1bc2fc4b168a34babbac4b27c6%2Fspectrum-261115-11.png" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>The duo sees good things ahead for Spectrum now that it’s based in Chicago.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Mark Black for the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>It’s a complementary partnership. Esposito does the administration, arranging bookings and grants, and serving as the outward-facing half of the duo. Goldberg takes on the most technically difficult music. “When [Esposito] first pitched joining the ensemble to me, they said to me, ‘You’re the talent. I’m the business,’” Goldberg said. “I actually said, ‘Jaime, you are also the talent!’”</p><p>The duo sees good things ahead for Spectrum now that it’s based in Chicago. “We didn’t really get gigs in Texas very often, unless it was, like, Fort Worth Pride,” Esposito said. “So I really hope this just creates a lot of opportunity.”</p><p>They’ve already booked a partnership with groups called Trans Composers Project and Queer Music Midwest for 45 minutes of newly commissioned music for percussion duo, scheduled for premiere in March 2027, tentatively in Chicago.</p><p>It promises to be a showcase for the queer music community in its full fabulousness, a community that is here making art for everyone all the time — not just during Pride Month.</p>

entries.title: Bears stadium bill in the red zone for Illinois lawmakers' fall veto session
entries.summary: <p>Illinois lawmakers will line up in Springfield this week for their goal line stand to block the Chicago Bears from rushing off to Indiana.</p><p>At least, that’s the game plan heading into the fall veto session, as legislators hope to finally pass a bill to help the team build a new stadium in their home state — whether that’s in Arlington Heights or the city the Bears have represented for more than a century.</p><p>Gov. JB Pritzker and his General Assembly allies have expressed <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/10/19/chicago-bears-stadium-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-gubernatorial-election-arlington-heights-chicago-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>as much confidence as ever</u></a> that the Bears’ five-year stadium flirtation is nearing a conclusion.</p><p>But the team remains as noncommittal as ever, weighing its suburban option versus two potential sites in Hammond, Indiana, plus a parade of revamped Chicago-based proposals the Bears have previously dismissed.</p><p>While that political football will eat up much of the Capitol play clock beginning Tuesday, legislators will also make a drive to pass new regulations on data centers, and even more tussling will happen behind closed doors as House Democrats maneuver to succeed outgoing Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch.</p><p>The first week of session is scheduled through Thursday before lawmakers finish out their calendar Dec. 1-3. Here’s what to watch for:</p><h3><b>Bears back on the clock</b></h3><p>Momentum has built behind one of the two Illinois bills that emerged in a frenzied but fruitless stadium push <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/05/31/bears-stadium-bill-springfield-arlington-heights-hammond-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>late in the spring session</u></a>, the most recent Springfield shutout that prompted the Bears to publicly shift their focus to Hammond.</p><p>With stadium negotiators all but trashing the framework the Bears had long sought — discounted payments in lieu of taxes to local governments (PILOT) — the sides have coalesced behind a municipal stadium authority model that would allow Chicago and Arlington Heights to lure the Bears and negotiate terms of a publicly owned stadium.</p><p>“There has been good progress made on a bill that would create a site-neutral and franchise-neutral approach to settling the stadium question,” said state Sen. Bill Cunningham, the South Side Democrat who serves as his chamber’s top stadium negotiator.</p><p>Cunningham spearheaded the initial version of the bill that passed the Senate but never got a House vote in the waning overnight hours of the spring session.</p><p>The municipal authority model gives Chicago a shot at keeping the Bears — and perhaps more importantly, gives Chicago legislators political cover to support a bill that could ultimately send the team to the suburbs.</p><p>While evaluating the Hammond sites — and testing the patience of Hoosier lawmakers who rolled out the navy-and-orange carpet with a generous taxpayer-funded stadium law signed <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/02/26/bears-stadium-hammond-indiana-hammong-senate-passes-bill-27-arlington-heights-george-mccaaskey-kevin-warren-nfl" target="_blank" ><u>in February</u></a> — the Bears’ Illinois talks have progressed since bringing minority owner Pat Ryan and NFL commissioner <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/06/bears-stadium-roger-goodell-nfl-commissioner-george-mccaskey-kevin-warren-chicago-arlington-heights-meeting-hammond-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>Roger Goodell</u></a> to the table over the summer.</p><p>Not that Illinois leaders are anywhere near victory formation. Negotiators don’t expect to vote on a bill until the second half of the session — and wouldn’t be surprised if it gets punted to the lame-duck session after the holidays.</p><p>“Getting agreement between all the parties is less important than getting members of the General Assembly comfortable with any kind of approach,” Cunningham said. “That’s the consensus that has to occur.”</p><p>A Bears spokesman pointed to the team’s most recent declaration they “appreciate the recent engagement from Illinois leadership” and “expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams [including Indiana] in the coming weeks.”</p><p>The team still has reservations about the state's commitment to funding public infrastructure upgrades around a potential stadium, upwards of $800 million that would be doled out incrementally over several state budget cycles. Meanwhile, suburban officials in Palatine and Rolling Meadows are demanding a seat at the table for Arlington Heights' potential municipal stadium authority, since their towns would neighbor the dome.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-710000" name="image-710000"></a> <picture class="Figure-credit"><p>Provided by Inference</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The Bears aren't behind any of the three glitzy Chicago stadium proposals that different developers have pitched in recent weeks: the former Michael Reese Hospital site in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/11/12/michael-reese-hospital-developers-10-billion-stadium-bears" target="_blank" ><u>Bronzeville</u></a>; the former U.S. Steel South Works site on the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/other-views/2026/06/22/bears-south-side-hammond-should-beat-arlington-heights-nfl-state-rep-curtis-tarver" target="_blank" ><u>Southeast Side</u></a>; or a bid to replace the White Sox’ home at Rate Field near <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/10/28/bridgeport-bears-domed-stadium-proposal-sox-rate-field" target="_blank" ><u>Bridgeport</u></a>.</p><p>Yet another proposal unaffiliated with the team is expected to surface soon, a revamped take on the lakefront dome south of Soldier Field the Bears <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2024/04/23/bears-new-stadium-dome-lakefront-soldier-field" target="_blank" ><u>pitched in 2024</u></a> with Mayor Brandon Johnson but was almost immediately shot down by Springfield due to its hefty public price tag.</p><p>Johnson’s office hasn’t yet endorsed a specific city proposal, but the “bottom line is that the mayor knows that Chicago is and should remain the home of the Bears and will continue to work with stakeholders across the region to make it so,” a spokesperson said in an email.</p><h3><b>Dealing with data centers</b></h3><p>Aside from Bears legislation, Gov. Pritzker said his top veto session agenda item is passing new data center regulations amid increasing concerns over data centers' impact on residential water and energy bills.</p><p>He and his General Assembly allies will aim to pass the Protecting Our Water, Energy and Ratepayers Act, or <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/10/22/data-centers-comed-3-billion-icc-consumer-groups-cub-illinois-households" target="_blank" ><u>POWER Act</u></a>, which would require data center developers to pay 100% of their costs before connecting to the grid. The bill languished at the end of May.</p><p>“We have a bill that would curtail the use of any outside electricity, and instead require data centers to bring their own electricity with them — clean energy, and also require them to use closed water systems,” Pritzker said earlier this month. “It should be up to local communities, whether or not they want a data center.”</p><h3><b>Speaker’s race</b></h3><p>The election’s over, but the politicking hasn’t stopped behind the scenes following Speaker Welch’s announcement he won’t seek a fourth term with the gavel, in the wake of a mutiny of caucus members who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/11/12/illinois-house-speaker-emanuel-chris-welch-accusations-domestic-abuse-lawsuits-patronage-proviso-district" target="_blank" ><u>criticized</u></a> his handling of sexual harassment allegations against ex-state Rep. Harry Benton.</p><p>Several <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/springfield/2026/11/06/illinois-house-speaker-chris-welch-steps-down-female-replacement-contenders" target="_blank" ><u>ambitious House Democrats</u></a> are already making calls to their colleagues seeking their support, though it’s not clear when a vote will happen to select the supermajority caucus’ leader come January, when the 105th General Assembly is sworn in.</p><p>Downtown state Rep. Kam Buckner has publicly<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fran-spielman-show/2026/11/11/kam-buckner-illinois-house-speaker-candidate-emanuel-chris-welch-ouster-harry-benton" > tossed his hat </a>in the ring, while other clout-heavy names are being floated, including state Reps. Eva-Dina Delgado, Jehan Gordon-Booth, Lisa Hernandez, Ann Williams, Marcus Evans and Jay Hoffman.</p>

entries.title: Voter turnout dropped in Chicago's GOP strongholds, increased in areas affected by Operation Midway Blitz
entries.summary: <p>Traditional Republican strongholds in Chicago saw a decrease in voter turnout in the Nov. 3 election, while areas affected by Operation Midway Blitz saw a bump.</p><p>WBEZ and the Chicago Sun-Times examined the 90 precincts President Donald Trump won in 2024, which represent traditionally conservative areas of the city. Voter turnout in those precincts was down an average of 6.26 percentage points in the November election compared to 2022.</p><p>And traditionally Democratic precincts that voted for Kamala Harris saw an increase in voter turnout by an average of 3.23 percentage points.</p><p>The analysis is based on election results posted by the Chicago Board of Election Commissioners as of Friday afternoon.</p><p>At the same time, data shows voter turnout was up in neighborhoods affected by Operation Midway Blitz, including in Little Village, Pilsen, Humboldt Park and the South Shore neighborhood. During the height of the immigration enforcement, 3,841 people were detained. Only 15% of those detained had a criminal conviction.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-400000" name="html-embed-module-400000"></a><div class="cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper"> <div class="cpm-gfx-embed"> <div style="min-height:789px" id="datawrapper-vis-DlEku"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/DlEku/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-DlEku"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/DlEku/full.png" alt="Choropleth map" /></noscript></div> </div> <div class="cpm-gfx-embed"> <div style="min-height:772px" id="datawrapper-vis-yoOWW"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/yoOWW/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-yoOWW"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/yoOWW/full.png" alt="Choropleth map" /></noscript></div> </div> </div> <style> .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper { align-items: start; display: flex; flex-direction: row; gap: 2rem; } .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper .cpm-gfx-embed { flex: 1; min-width: 18rem; } @media screen and (max-width: 30rem) { .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper { align-items: stretch; flex-direction: column; gap: 0; } } </style> </div> </div><p>In the South Shore raid on Sept. 30, 2025, allegedly acting on a <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/housing/2026/01/22/residents-long-suspected-feds-south-shore-raid-tip-came-from-landlord-now-under-state-investigation-immigration-bovino-border-patrol-ice" target="_blank" ><u>tip from building management</u></a>, federal agents rappelled down from helicopters, ransacked the building and zip-tied residents, many of them U.S. citizens. Government officials said they were going after members of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, but no criminal charges have been filed against anyone arrested that night.</p><p>In the 7th Ward, where federal agents raided the South Shore building, voter turnout was up 5.3 percentage points.</p><p>In Little Village and surrounding neighborhoods, home to the 22nd Ward, all precincts saw an increase in voter turnout except for the precinct that is home to the Cook County Jail, which saw a drop of 6.5 percentage points compared to the 2022 midterms. Trump won that precinct in 2024. All precincts in Pilsen also saw increases in voter turnout.</p><p>All precincts in the 41st Ward on the Far Northwest Side also saw drops in voter turnout. The ward was the only in which Trump won more than half the votes in the November 2024 election.</p><p>Nearly all precincts in the 19th Ward, home to Beverly and Mount Greenwood, saw a double digit drop in voter turnout in the November election. The neighborhoods, home to police officers, firefighters and union workers, have historically shown support for GOP candidates.</p><h3><b>Blue gains across Illinois</b></h3><p>In Chicago, Trump jumped to 22.01% of the city vote in 2024, up from 12.41% of the city vote in 2016. In Illinois, Trump’s statewide vote grew to 45.3% in 2024, up from 38.76% in 2016, according to returns.</p><p>But the November election painted a picture of national dissatisfaction over Trump administration policies, including the war in Iran, which has directly impacted gas prices, as well as aggressive immigration efforts and general affordability issues affecting Americans.</p><p>With Democratic blowouts in favor of Gov. JB Pritzker, Attorney General Kwame Raoul, Comptroller-elect Margaret Croke and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/11/03/governor-illinois-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-results" target="_blank" ><u>all other statewide officeholders</u></a>, Illinois Republicans are finding themselves in dire straits.</p><p>Democrats even made inroads in territory long considered solid Republican ground, with Ricky Rivard unseating four-term GOP St. Charles state Rep. Dan Ugaste.</p><p>Rockford state Sen. Dave Syverson — the longest-serving member of the chamber, in office since 1993 — narrowly won against Democratic challenger Sarah Mertens, 50.8% to 49.2%.</p><p>Pritzker won his third term by his widest margin yet — 60.6% to Darren Bailey’s 36%. The Democratic governor also picked up red counties like Winnebago, McHenry, Sangamon and Jackson counties.</p><h3><b>Operation Midway Blitz a motivating factor</b></h3><p>Growing up in Little Village, Brenda Anaya said she grew accustomed to seeing the neighborhood bustling with people. But that changed when the Trump administration launched Operation Midway Blitz last fall.</p><p>As federal agents began filling the streets in search of undocumented immigrants, Anaya said residents grew fearful and stopped leaving their homes.</p><p>“A lot of people were scared,” said Anaya, 27. “It was a hard time for everyone living here.”</p><p>Anaya voted for Democrats in the midterm election and was confident they would win in Illinois. However, she was surprised to see Democratic victories extend beyond the state and across the country.</p><p>After Democrats gained control of both the U.S. Senate and U.S. House of Representatives during the midterm elections, Anaya said she’s beginning to hope things will return to normal.</p><p>“When [elected officials] come into office, I hope they do what they can to stop ICE,” she said.</p><p>Anaya hopes immigration enforcement will stop not only in Chicago but across the country.</p><p>“People should feel safe,” she said.</p>

entries.title: Police seek man who robbed passenger on CTA bus in Englewood
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are looking for a man who robbed and threatened a passenger on a CTA bus in Englewood in September.</p><p>The man approached the 23-year-old passenger while boarded on the bus in the 6600 block of South Halsted Street around 10:15 p.m. Sept. 15 and robbed him, police said. The 23-year-old wasn't injured.</p><p>The man, who police believe is around 25 years old, was last seen wearing a tan hat, blue shirt and dark pants with tan boots, officials said. He is about 5-foot-8 and weighs 150 pounds. </p><p>Anyone with information is encouraged to contact Public Transportation Detectives at 312-745-4447.</p>

class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-x/" target="_blank" >Christiana Freitag</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-m/" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-a/" target="_blank" >reporting fewer delays and cancellations early Monday</a> following <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-f/" target="_blank" >Friday’s nationwide ground stop</a> that led to hundreds of delays and cancellations and left thousands stranded over the weekend. The ground stop, which lasted more than four hours, was the longest in 25 years.</p><p><b>What happened</b>: Air travel was thrown into chaos across the country Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued the rare, nationwide ground stop. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-z/" target="_blank" >told reporters Saturday</a> a contractor had been replacing a section of the system's old copper wire with new fiber wire, and that work somehow caused a system overload.</p><p><b>Stranded travelers</b>: For <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-v/" target="_blank" >stranded travelers</a>, the disruption also came with mounting expenses, from unexpected hotel stays to repeated rebooking costs and the prospect of paying for alternative transportation.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-s/" target="_blank" ><b>READ MORE</b></a></p><hr><p></p><h4>LET’S HEAR FROM YOU 🗣️</h4><p><b>Were you affected by Friday's FAA ground stop? Now, courtesy of some fresh talent and an influx of grant dollars intended to use arts to catalyze community development, there’s a tentative new chapter emerging.</p><p>In Grand Crossing, eta Creative Arts Foundation now has a resident company, Pulse Theatre. In Hyde Park, across the street from the University of Chicago, Definition Theatre is laying out ambitions beyond its storefront. The company has also opened its doors to South Side itinerant theater groups. This fall, Perceptions Theater and Coalescence Theatre Project will stage Kelundra Smith's "Other Paths to God" at Definition.</p><p>A short walk away, Court Theatre on the U. of C. campus has become one of the premier Equity venues in the city — recently doing more to showcase the work of Black artists than it has in the past. The Beverly Arts Center, founded in 1967, is still staging plays; so is its former resident company, Beverly Theatre Guild, the oldest community theater company in Chicago.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydhklie-l-il/" target="_blank" >READ MORE</a></p><hr><p>Thanks for reading the Sun-Times Morning Edition! entries.title: Woman, 73, critically hurt when hit by SUV on Near North Side
entries.summary: <p>A 73-year-old woman was struck by an SUV Sunday night on the North Side. </p><p>The woman was on the street in the first block of West Maple Street around 5 p.m. when a Chevrolet SUV going east struck her, Chicago police said. </p><p>She was taken to Northwestern Memorial Hospital where she was in critical condition, police said.</p><p>The SUV driver, a 56-year-old man, was given citations for failing to reduce his speed and operating an uninsured vehicle, officials said. </p><p>The Major Accidents Investigations Unit was looking into the crash. </p>

entries.title: Blackhawks' key to success against easier stretch of opponents: Win puck battles
entries.summary: <p>It's pretty obvious now that the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> aren't going to become a winning team this season. They'll need to reconfigure important parts of their roster — and wait longer for their young players to develop and improve — before that happens.</p><p>In the immediate short-term, though, the Hawks do have some opportunities for potential wins that could at least make their record (currently 5-13-2) more respectable.</p><p>Their next five opponents — the Maple Leafs, Blue Jackets, Flames, Canucks and Kraken — all entered Sunday among the bottom 10 teams in the NHL. The Hawks should have a legitimate chance against every one.</p><p>The stretch of opponents after Thanksgiving — the Rangers, Wild, Jets, Predators and Blues — isn't intimidating, either. Only one of their next 10 opponents made the playoffs last season.</p><p>Had the Hawks held onto their four-goal lead <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/14/blackhawks-jets-mark-scheifele-shutdown-forward-jason-dickinson" >Saturday</a> (or if Connor Bedard's double-post shot in overtime had gone in) and they entered this week on a two-game winning streak, there would probably be more optimism. That meltdown was a gut punch.</p><p>But the Hawks can still reflect what they did well <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/12/blackhawks-sabres-defensive-structure-ryan-donato-patrick-kane" >in their win Thursday</a> against the Sabres — as well as in the first period against the Jets — as keys moving forward.</p><p>One crucial thing: winning puck battles.</p><p>The Hawks entered Thursday ranked second-last in the league in terms of percentage of puck battles won. Then they dominated the Sabres, producing the highest puck-battle win percentage of any team in any game this season, per Sportlogiq director Mike Kelly.</p><p>Visually, they looked OK in battles against the Jets, too. Ryan Donato was an individual standout, winning some battles to set up Anton Frondell's first-period goal and winning some more during the Hawks' ill-fated attempt to hold their lead through the third period.</p><p>But Sportlogiq tracked the Hawks as winning only 38% of battles in total, per Kelly, which marked a crash back down to earth.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Ryan Donato won several battles to create this Anton Frondell goal Saturday: <a href="https://t.co/4liMzh6esq">pic.twitter.com/4liMzh6esq</a></p>— Ben Pope’s Video Clips (@BenPopeCSTclips) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCSTclips/status/2122106229195698194?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 15, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Hawks need more possession time, and winning battles is a critical way to get the puck. It's easy to understand their importance.</p><p>It's harder to actually win them, though. The Hawks do have some scrappy guys with high work ethic. But they also lack size within their forward group and physicality within their defensive corps.</p><p>Coach Jeff Blashill said the Hawks do closely monitor their own puck-battle analytics and that "athleticism, strength on puck, desire, compete" are all factors in winning them.</p><p>Said Frondell: "You have to do the off-ice work to be strong, to not fall over — you want to have good balance — but also [you have to do] technical stuff, get momentum, get in front of him, use your stick in different ways. Just stick-on-puck and body contact is a good way."</p><p>It would also behoove the Hawks to remember the details they practiced last week and maintain their tightened-up forechecking structure moving forward.</p><p>After getting slaughtered by odd-man rushes most of this season, they conceded only a few to the Sabres and Jets. That will be another key to success during this easier stretch.</p>

entries.title: Metra's holiday train tickets go on sale Monday
entries.summary: <p>Tickets for Metra's holiday trains will go on sale at noon Monday. </p><p>Specially decorated trains with holiday characters will make round trips on the BNSF, Milwaukee District North, and Rock Island lines on Dec. 5, the UP Northwest Line on Dec. 12, and the UP North Line on Dec. 19, according to Metra. </p><p>On the Metra Electric Line, the decorated trains will take riders to a "winter wonderland" at Millennium Station featuring games, treats, Santa, and other activities Dec. 12, 13, and 19.</p><p>The tickets, which are selling on <a class="Link" href="https://metra.com/holidaytrains" target="_blank" >Metra’s website</a> for $10, are expected to sell out fast. Tickets are limited to five per purchase. <br></p>

entries.title: Chicago musicians from Mavis Staples to Kurt Elling to Ye land nods on 2027 Grammy Awards list
entries.summary: <p>Chicagoans from <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/music/2025/11/08/mavis-staples-provides-solace-for-our-sad-and-beautiful-world-in-new-album" target="_blank" ><u>Mavis Staples</u></a> to former First Lady Michelle Obama, poet J. Ivy and the controversial rap star <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/music/2026/09/03/kanye-west-ye-chicago-legacy-essays" target="_blank" ><u>Ye</u></a> all received Grammy nominations Monday morning.</p><p>Staples, the 87-year-old reigning queen of Americana music, received several nominations for music’s top prize. The nominations for her latest solo project, “Sad and Beautiful World,” include <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-american-roots-performance/" target="_blank" ><u>Best American Roots Performance</u></a>, <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-americana-performance/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Americana Performance</u></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-americana-album/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Americana Album</u></a>. The album is also up for <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-album-cover/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Album Cover</u></a>. This brings Staples’ all-time total to 19 Grammy nominations, including five wins.</p><p>Michelle Obama scored her third Grammy nomination in the <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-audio-book-narration-and-storytelling-recording/" target="_blank" ><u>audiobook category</u></a> for “The Look,” which chronicled her fashion while in the White House.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-ee0000" name="image-ee0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a0ed0ad/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+0/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F29%2Fda%2Fd82f2bcb4956a7411eebc22f0c56%2Fjivy-012723-19.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b78e5ff/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+0/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F29%2Fda%2Fd82f2bcb4956a7411eebc22f0c56%2Fjivy-012723-19.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/9fce31a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/3000x1684+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F29%2Fda%2Fd82f2bcb4956a7411eebc22f0c56%2Fjivy-012723-19.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="J. Hathaway is also up for <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-traditional-rb-performance/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Traditional R&B Performance</u></a>.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/music/2026/11/12/andrew-bird-20-year-anniversary-mysterious-production-of-eggs-cso" target="_blank" ><u>Andrew Bird</u></a>, the multi-instrumentalist indie artist from the northern suburbs who just made his debut with the Chicago Symphony Orchestra this past weekend, is nominated <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-song-written-for-visual-media/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Song Written For Visual Media</u></a> for his song “Need Someone,” written for the HBO hospital drama "The Pitt.”</p><p>The latest project from Ye, the artist formerly known as Kanye West, titled “BULLY - DELUXE” is nominated for <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-rap-album/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Rap Album</u></a>. And Chicagoan <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/music/2026/05/01/chicago-international-jazz-day-pope-leo-herbie-hancock-kurt-elling-lyric-opera" target="_blank" ><u>Kurt Elling</u></a> is up And Marin Alsop, who long led the Chicago Symphony Orchestra during the summer months at Ravinia, is nominated for <a class="Link" href="https://www.grammy.com/awards/categories/best-orchestral-performance/2027/" target="_blank" ><u>Best Orchestral Performance</u></a> for conducting the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra.</p><p>This year’s slate of Grammy contenders is dominated by women, with British songwriter Raye and Spanish singer <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/rosalia" target="_blank" ><u>Rosalía</u></a> leading with the most nods. Raye <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/grammy-nominations-2027-list-a481a68c0754c0f8a0425c508c0304c5" target="_blank" ><u>is up for 11 awards</u></a> at February’s ceremony: record, song and album of the year — the first time she’s been nominated in those big categories — as well as songwriter of the year non-classical, a variety of pop categories and music video.</p><p>Her 11 nods also mean she has tied <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/beyonce-knowles" target="_blank" ><u>Beyoncé’s</u></a> record at the 2025 Grammys for the most nominations in a single year by a female artist.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/rosalia" target="_blank" ><u>Spanish singer Rosalía</u></a>, fresh off her album of the year win at the 27th annual <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/latin-grammy-awards" target="_blank" ><u>Latin Grammy Awards</u></a> on Thursday for <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/rosalia-lux-music-review-e303383da29b880fc9eda5efbdd7bc80" target="_blank" ><u>her avant-garde “Lux,”</u></a> follows Raye with nine nominations. She’s a first-time nominee in all the categories she’s up for: record, song and album of the year as well as pop solo performance, alternative music performance, alternative music album, Latin song, global music performance and music video.</p><p>Following her are Miranda Lambert, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/music/2026/10/13/review-olivia-rodrigo-unraveled-tour-united-center-chicago" >Olivia Rodrigo</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/music/2026/09/20/review-phoebe-bridgers-the-lost-tour-united-center" >Phoebe Bridgers</a> and first-time nominee Ella Langley, who are tied with seven nods each.</p><p>Bruno Mars, Leon Thomas and 2026’s <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/grammy-best-new-artist-2026-bd221f7168ae909204ddbddbb819859a" target="_blank" ><u>best new artist winner Olivia Dean</u></a> have six nominations each.</p><p>Recordings commercially released in the U.S. between Aug. 31, 2025, and Aug. 28, 2026, were eligible for nominations. The final round of Grammy voting, which determines the winners, will take place between Dec. 10 and Jan. 7. </p><p>The 2027 Grammy Awards will air Feb. 7 at 7 p.m. Eastern, live on ABC for the first time since 1972, from the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. It will also stream on Disney+ and Hulu.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-3c0000" entries.title: Trabajadores de tres hoteles más se suman a la huelga por mejores sueldos en Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Cientos de trabajadores de tres hoteles prominentes de Chicago se han sumado a una huelga en curso por mejores sueldos y prestaciones, anunció el sindicato el domingo.</p><p>Los trabajadores de Marriott Marquis, Royal Sonesta y The Wade Hotel, representados por el sindicato UNITE HERE Local 1, se declararon en huelga el domingo.</p><p>Cientos de trabajadores más en el Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk, Waldorf Astoria Chicago, Palmer House, un hotel de Hilton, The Westin Chicago River North, Westin Michigan Avenue, Millennium Hotel Knickerbocker, Hilton Chicago y Hyatt Regency Chicago ya han estado en huelga este otoño, muchos de ellos desde mediados de octubre, cuando comenzaron las huelgas en seis hoteles antes del Maratón de Chicago.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-cb0000" name="module-cb0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Los trabajadores dicen que están sobrecargados de trabajo y que no reciben un pago justo, y esperan que la huelga impulse avances en la mesa de negociación.</p><p>"No quiero estar en huelga, especialmente con este frío", dijo María Jiménez, personal de limpieza en el Royal Sonesta. "Pero esto es lo que tenemos que hacer. Nosotros, los trabajadores, mantenemos los hoteles en funcionamiento, y aún así no es suficiente para estas empresas. No nos están respetando en la mesa de negociación".</p><p>Los empleados hoteleros enfrentan apuros económicos, según el sindicato, con alrededor de un tercio de los afiliados que reportan tener dificultades para cubrir la renta y los servicios, según una encuesta de 2025 realizada por el sindicato. Los contratos con Hyatt, Marriott y Hilton expiraron el 31 de agosto.</p><p>Royal Sonesta y Marriott, que opera el Marriott Marquis y The Wade Hotel, no respondieron de inmediato a solicitudes de comentario.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Police release photos after 2 separate attacks on CTA property in Loop, South Loop
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police have released photos of attackers in two separate incidents on CTA property in the Loop and South Loop. </p><p>Around 5:35 a.m. Nov. 11, a 29-year-old woman was walking on the train platform stairs in the 1100 block of South State Street when she was pushed to the ground, police said. </p><p>The attacker, believed to be a man between 20 and 30 with a thin entries.title: At Pilsen's Mexican art museum, 50 people take oath of U.S. citizenship
entries.summary: <p>After taking the oath of allegiance Monday morning, Roberto Flores stayed at the National Museum of Mexican Art with his fiancée to walk through its galleries.</p><p>For Flores, 49, the ceremony was especially meaningful. He came to the United States from Michoacán when he was 2, grew up in Pilsen and Little Village, and has held a green card since 1990.</p><p>“It’s a great thing they’re doing here,” Flores said. “I'm proud to be Mexican too, as I am an American now."</p><p>Flores was among 50 people from 24 countries who became U.S. citizens Monday at the museum, including 16 from Mexico, according to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois. It was the first time the museum had hosted a naturalization ceremony in its 44-year history.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure </div><p>The museum, 1852 W 19th St., was founded by educators seeking to help young Mexican Americans stay connected to their cultural roots, said President and CEO José Ochoa. It was envisioned as a place where immigrants could build lives in the United States while maintaining a connection to their heritage.</p><p>“We can still be where we're from. And we can still be from here,” Ochoa told the new citizens.</p><p>For Rosario Lara, 73, who lives in Brighton Park, citizenship meant an opportunity to participate more fully in her community. Originally from Mexico City, Lara said she had been a permanent resident for 16 years before becoming a citizen.</p><p>“I want to serve my community, and I want to vote,” she said through a family member who helped translate.</p><p>U.S. Rep. Jesús “Chuy” García, who immigrated from Mexico as a child, also addressed the new citizens. He recalled arriving in the neighborhood in 1965 with his mother and siblings.</p><p>“Let us never forget that this nation was built by immigrants,” García said.</p><p>The ceremony was administered by Chief Judge Virginia M. entries.title: Will preseason No. 1 Neuqua Valley win Naperville its first boys basketball state championship?
entries.summary: <p>Two of the best basketball players in Neuqua Valley history arrived in high school at basically the same time, and it may lead to a special winter in south Naperville.</p><p>Junior Cole Kelly and senior Mason Martin are talking about winning a state title. Kelly is very clear: “Anything short of Champaign is not a good season for us.”</p><p>Kelly, a 6-7 guard, has offers from much of the Big Ten and is a top-100 player in the country, according to 247sports.com. He averaged 20 points, 8 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 steals while shooting 52% from the field last season.</p><p>But the numbers aren’t important. Kelly, already a two-time Sun-Times All-Area selection, is one of the state’s two superstars. As he showed in Neuqua Valley’s win against Bolingbrook and Brady Pettigrew (the other superstar) last season at When Sides Collide, he can change a game all by himself.</p><p>Kelly shouldn’t have to do that too often thanks to Martin, an Illinois recruit. The 6-5 senior is the area’s best three-point shooter and has improved his all-around game over the summer. Martin averaged 20 points and four rebounds last season.</p><p>The Wildcats don’t resemble a traditional preseason No. 1 team. There are two stars and a supporting cast of capable high school basketball players. This isn’t a super team, but that doesn’t exist in the state this season.</p><p>“I never thought [the preseason No. 1] would happen in my life,” Neuqua Valley coach Todd Sutton said. “The [Public League] teams were usually the best in the country, and they were special. I told my son [assistant coach Tyler Sutton], this is the only time it is going to happen, so let's enjoy it for a week or two.”</p><p>Sutton, the only coach in school history, could crack the 600-win mark this season. Neuqua Valley advanced to supersectionals in 2008 and 2009 but has never been to state. No Naperville high school has won a boys basketball state championship. Naperville Central is the only team to advance to the finals, and that was in 1915.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a Wildcats need the supporting cast to step up considerably this season. The pieces are in place. Starters Carter Coviello and Danny Mikuta both return. Luke Balgro, a 6-4 senior, impressed when he returned from injury late last season. Experienced guard Arshil Khimani's three-point shot improved over the summer. Senior guard Bryson Pierre and 6-7 junior Hunter Rheaume will also contribute.</p><p>“I want to be more of a threat to score,” Coviello said. “If the role players can be more of a threat, it makes it so much easier for us to win games. That will be a big key to our season, the rest of us being able to improve offensively.”</p><p>Notice that Coviello refers to himself as a role player. That may be Neuqua Valley’s hidden strength. This is a true team. Chemistry is high; the players grew up together and understand and accept their roles.</p><p>“The starting five meshes together and everyone on the team knows what they are doing,” Kelly said. “I saw a lot of good things from the younger guys this summer. They aren't necessarily out there to do anything special: keep the ball, rebound and play some defense. But they are able to step up if someone is in foul trouble.”</p><p>The Wildcats will play in most major local events and the prestigious Highland Shootout near St. Louis in early January.</p><p>“The way last season ended just left a bad taste in our mouth,” Coviello said. “Obviously, our goal is to win it all. We want to be champs, and we talk about it a lot.”</p>

entries.title: Navy identifies 21-year-old sailor found dead in West Loop
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police detectives continue Monday to investigate the death of a 21-year-old U.S. Navy sailor found in the West Loop neighborhood earlier this month, the Navy confirmed.</p><p>Seaman Jack D. Jacobs was found unresponsive outside in the 600 block of West Wayman Street around 8 p.m. Nov. 7, according to the Chicago Police Department. </p><p>Jacobs, who was pronounced dead at the scene, was assigned as a student to the Surface Combat Systems Training Command Great Lakes, according to Matt Mogle, spokesperson for Naval Station Great Lakes in North Chicago and the Cook County medical examiner's office. </p><p>Jacobs was identified by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service at the medical examiner’s office on Nov. 10, Mogle said in a statement.</p><p>“The Navy mourns the loss of our shipmate and extends our deepest condolences to his family, friends, and fellow Sailors during this difficult time,” Mogle said in a statement.</p><p>An autopsy was inconclusive and pending further studies, according to the medical examiner's office and Chicago police detectives are leading the investigation. </p>
