entries.title: Ben Johnson needs to find explosive run plays — and Kyle Monangai will help
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ run game is deliberate but not dangerous.</p><p>Getting Kyle Monangai back Sunday against the Saints will help, but the running back alone isn’t the solution. Rather, coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/15/bears-nfc-north-proved-nasty-sunday-vikings-packers-lions-ben-johnson" target="_blank" >Ben Johnson</a> spent the bye week trying to find ways, both with scheme and personnel, to manufacture explosive run plays.</p><p>“We're very open about what we've got to work on,” Monangai, who is on pace to return from a Week 4 turf toe injury, said after practice Monday. “We know we've got a lot more to get in the run game. This week will be about getting back on track and getting it right back in the right direction to where we know we're capable of.”</p><p>The Bears have reason to believe in Johnson’s ability to adjust during the bye week. His Lions offenses scored 41 points after their 2023 bye and 47 after their 2024 bye. Last year, the Bears scored 25.</p><p>When the Bears took their Week 5 bye last year, they were averaging 3.8 yards per carry, the seventh-worst mark in the NFL. Their longest carry had gone for 20 yards. From Week 6 on, the Bears led the NFL with 5.2 yards per carry. D’Andre Swift, who averaged 3.3 yards per rush before the bye, averaged 5.4 after it. Monangai, who averaged 3.6 before the bye, averaged 4.7 after it.</p><p>“There were some things coming out of last year’s bye week that we were able to lean into,” Johnson said last week. “And I’m hoping we’re going to be able to find some nuggets like that of just areas that we really can make it more consistent.”</p><p>Monday, the Bears focused on fixing the mistakes they made in the first half of the season. Tuesday, Johnson will begin rolling out fixes he found when the Bears begin implementing their game plan. He might have a willing opponent Sunday — the Saints give up 129.6 yards per game, the sixth-most in the NFL.</p><p>NFL teams average 4.2 yards per carry this year. So do the Bears. Johnson runs the ball a league-high 33.7 times per game, though, which is why the Bears’ 142 yards per contest ranks fourth in the league.</p><p>Different teams have different definitions for explosive plays, but, generally, they’re 20-yard pass plays and 10-yard run plays. The Bears have 26 such rushes this season, which is tied for 14<sup>th</sup>-most in the NFL.</p><p>In Week 9, the longest carry by a Bears running back went for eight yards.</p><p>In Week 8, it was nine.</p><p>In Week 7, it was 10.</p><p>“It always comes down to us making the backs’ reads clear and concise so they’re not second-guessing things,” right guard Jonah Jackson said. “We’re excited for the challenge. We got some good defenses ahead that know how to attack us. We’ll figure out ways to get around it.”</p><p>Right tackle Darnell Wright was more succinct when asked what could unlock longer runs.</p><p>“Sustaining through the play, everybody getting their assisgnments,” he said.</p><p>There have been 57 rushing plays of 30 yards or more in the NFL this season. Just two belong to Bears running backs — a Monangai 61-yard touchdown and a 32-yard Swift run. Both were in Week 1.</p><p>“I’ve got to look at is it the fact that we’re not getting as many explosives in the run game right now,” Johnson said. “Is that why the average is low? Or is it, we’re just not moving the line of scrimmage?”</p><p>The advanced stats paint their run game as average. They rank 20<sup>th</sup> in team rushing yards over expected per play. They’re 16<sup>th</sup> in rushing yards before contact per play and 13<sup>th</sup> in yards after contact.</p><p>More rudimentary numbers say the same. The Bears have averaged more than four yards per carry in just three games this season.</p><p>“Which, simply in our terms, it’s just not good enough right now,” Johnson said. “And those guys know that. Particularly as the weather continues to turn into Bear weather, we’re going to need to lean on that run game more — and it’s going to need to come through for us.”</p><p>The Bears boast three of the same starting offensive linemen that created lanes for their running backs all last year. A fourth, left tackle Theo Benedet, started eight games last year.</p><p>They have Monangai back, too, after he missed more time to injury than at any point in his football career, at any level. When he returns, he’ll wear a right cleat with special protection for his toe, which he said he can successfully manage the rest of the season.</p><p>But, more importantly, the Bears have Johnson, who likes to boast that no team adjusts better than his staff. To get more explosive runs, they'll have to.</p><p>“I have all the confidence,” Monangai said. “It will show on Sunday but … it's a work in progress.”</p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: ‘Definitely’ interested in Clay Holmes, how will Cubs remake pitching staff amid Tarik Skubal sweepstakes?
entries.summary: <p>As he stood on a box speaking to a throng of gathered media, the phone of baseball’s highest profile agent went off.</p><p>“Just another owner begging to meet with [Tarik] Skubal,” Scott Boras said to laughs.</p><p>What are the chances it was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> chairman Tom Ricketts calling?</p><p>Though they shelled out $175 million for Boras client Alex Bregman last winter, the Cubs have a reputation — at least among frustrated fans — as a big-market team that doesn’t always spend like one.</p><p>Not helping to shatter that narrative, the Cubs launching themselves into the Skubal sweepstakes doesn’t seem likely this winter, even as Jed Hoyer’s front office seeks to remake the North Side pitching staff and get closer to competing with the world-champion Brewers in the NL Central.</p><p>Skubal, a two-time Cy Young winner, would be the ultimate top-of-the-rotation arm, a one-of-a-kind ace to counter the Brewers’ Jacob Misiorowski.</p><p>There’s one person, at least, who sees forking over gargantuan green for his services as a good investment.</p><p>“All these true No. 1's, they’ve all led to world championships,” Boras said Wednesday during the GM meetings. “Over a 30- or 40-year period, we might have 10 of these aces that are capable of winning multiple Cy Youngs. And what that means is they have the ability to allow a franchise to clearly have an opportunity to win a coveted world championship.”</p><p>Boras shied away from addressing the Cubs too specifically. When asked about them and the White Sox making expensive signings this offseason, he agreed it’d be a good idea, no surprise coming from the guy whose job it is to land those kinds of deals for his players.</p><p>“It’s rare you have two baseball playoff teams [in Chicago] at the same time. So I would say, they have every reason to advance, they have every reason to say prosperity’s at their doorstep,” he said. “To not do so would be something that is going to allow them to step back … and I don’t think that’s in any way going to help their fan base or what they’ve worked so hard to build.</p><p>“I fully expect that anybody who truly wants to win … your fans are going to grade them by the pursuits of the best players on the market, or lack thereof.”</p><p>Skubal might be too much for the Cubs in an offseason where they need to bring in a lot more than just one pitcher. All five arms who finished the season in the rotation are free agents, and most of the in-house candidates to replace them are coming off significant injuries.</p><p>But might one or more of those guys who went from the Cubs’ rotation to free agency wind up making a return trip to the North Side?</p><p>The Cubs are interested in bringing back righty Clay Holmes, general manager Carter Hawkins said Tuesday, a reunion that makes an awful lot of sense considering why the team gave up their No. 2 prospect to add Holmes to a contending roster at the trade deadline.</p><p>“Clay’s got great stuff,” Hawkins said. “He puts the ball on the ground. … He’s a really good fit with our club, with the fact that we have such good infield defense. There’s some nice synergy there.</p><p>“He’s definitely somebody we’ll have interest in.”</p><p>Holmes’ status as a ground-ball specialist fits perfectly with a Cubs infield boasting a trio of Gold Glove winners.</p><p>Though he didn’t deliver what the Cubs hoped he would — after dazzling by allowing just one run during a four-start stretch shortly after being acquired, he had an 8.24 ERA in four September outings, issuing 15 walks in fewer than 20 innings, and didn’t pitch in the playoffs — he remains that perfect fit and someone with a long track record of success.</p><p>Acquired in a trade with the same team, the Mets, more than a month before Holmes, lefty David Peterson makes similar sense as someone who could return to the Cubs’ rotation.</p><p>Like Holmes, Peterson has a reputation as one of baseball’s best ground-ball generators, and the 2025 All Star did some of his best pitching at season’s end, allowing just three runs over his final four starts of the regular season. Unlike Holmes, Peterson did see playoff action, tossing a scoreless 1⅔ innings in Game 2 against the Padres.</p><p>Whether either pitcher fits what the Cubs are trying to do financially remains to be seen, and the looming lockout figures to throw an awful lot about the offseason into question.</p><p>But if the Cubs aren’t going to buy what Boras is selling and add Skubal to a Midwestern arms race with the Brewers, reuniting with Holmes and/or Peterson could be their strategy to close a massive gap in the division.</p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase triggers online banking delays across major US banks
entries.summary: <p>NEW YORK (AP) — Thousands of customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks Monday, after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.</p><p>However, Chase said Monday that the technical problems were not the result of a cyberattack, and that they were working to bring banking services back online.</p><p>“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”</p><p>The disruption comes days after there were <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/flights-grounded-microsoft-ai-chaos-ea5f7a1f95a38f65dd57e58cfc17672b" target="_blank" >two major outages</a> affecting other parts of the economy: A <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/microsoft-outage-outlook-email-365-recover-ca395c0f1e51af784b6d70afb6554f6a" target="_blank" >major outage by Microsoft</a> happened Friday and lasted for hours, severely impacting services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot. This was followed by an outage with the FAA, which <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/flights-halted-airports-faa-f81b0904331dafad6133f291e5f531a8" target="_blank" >grounded all U.S. flights</a> for several hours this weekend.</p><p>The technical issues seem to be centered at Chase customers and customers at other banks who are trying to transact with Chase. Other banks, including Bank of America and Citigroup, were not having issues with their banking services on Monday.</p><p>A spokesman for U.S. Bank said its systems are not directly impacted but that “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”</p><p>Zelle is the peer-to-peer payment system that major U.S. banks use to allow customers to send money to friends and family at near-instant speed. Zelle is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which in turn is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo.</p><p>A spokesman for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was fully operational.</p><p>“An issue at the financial institutions may be delaying Zelle payments for some of their customers,” the spokesman said.</p><p>Some Chase customers received a message that said “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”</p>
entries.author: Ken Sweet

entries.title: Participación electoral subió en áreas afectadas por el Operativo Midway Blitz y cayó en los distritos republicanos de Chicago
entries.summary: <p>Los bastiones republicanos tradicionales en Chicago registraron una caída en la participación electoral en la elección del 3 de noviembre, mientras que las áreas afectadas por el Operativo Midway Blitz registraron un aumento.</p><p>WBEZ y el Chicago Sun-Times examinaron los 90 precintos que el presidente Donald Trump ganó en 2024, que representan áreas tradicionalmente conservadoras de la ciudad. La participación electoral en esos precintos bajó un promedio de 6.26 puntos porcentuales en la elección de noviembre en comparación con 2022.</p><p>Y los precintos tradicionalmente demócratas que votaron por Kamala Harris registraron un aumento en la participación electoral de un promedio de 3.23 puntos porcentuales.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-910000" name="module-910000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>El análisis se basa en los resultados electorales publicados por la Junta de Comisionados Electorales de Chicago hasta la tarde del viernes.</p><p>Al mismo tiempo, los datos muestran que la participación electoral subió en vecindarios afectados por el Operativo Midway Blitz, incluyendo La Villita, Pilsen, Humboldt Park y el vecindario de South Shore.</p><p>En el auge de las redadas migratorias fueron detenidas 3,841 personas. Solo el 15% de los detenidos tenía una condena penal.</p><p>En la redada en South Shore del 30 de septiembre de 2025, presuntamente actuando por una pista de la administración del edificio, agentes federales descendieron en rápel desde helicópteros, registraron a fondo el edificio y sujetaron con bridas a los residentes, muchos de ellos ciudadanos estadounidenses. Funcionarios dijeron que iban tras miembros de la pandilla venezolana Tren de Aragua, pero no se han presentado cargos penales contra nadie arrestado esa noche.</p><p>En el distrito político 7, donde agentes federales allanaron el edificio de South Shore, la participación electoral subió 5.3 puntos porcentuales.</p><p>En La Villita y los vecindarios circundantes, pertenecientes al distrito político 22, todos los precintos vieron un aumento en la participación electoral, excepto el precinto que alberga la Cárcel del Condado de Cook, que registró una caída de 6.5 puntos porcentuales en comparación con las elecciones de medio término de 2022. Trump ganó ese precinto en 2024.</p><p>Todos los precintos de Pilsen también registraron aumentos en la participación.</p><p>Todos los precintos del distrito político 41, en el lado extremo noroeste, también vieron descensos en la participación electoral. Ese distrito fue el único en el que Trump obtuvo más de la mitad de los votos en la elección de noviembre de 2024.</p><p>Casi todos los precintos del distrito político 19, que incluye los vecindarios de Beverly y Mount Greenwood, registraron una caída de doble dígito en la participación en la elección de noviembre. Esos vecindarios, hogar conocido de policías, bomberos y trabajadores sindicalizados, históricamente han mostrado apoyo a los candidatos republicanos.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-ca0000" name="html-embed-module-ca0000"></a><div class="cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper"> <div class="cpm-gfx-embed"> <div style="min-height:789px" id="datawrapper-vis-DlEku"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/DlEku/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-DlEku"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/DlEku/full.png" alt="Choropleth map" /></noscript></div> </div> <div class="cpm-gfx-embed"> <div style="min-height:772px" id="datawrapper-vis-yoOWW"><script type="text/javascript" defer src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/yoOWW/embed.js" charset="utf-8" data-target="#datawrapper-vis-yoOWW"></script><noscript><img src="https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/yoOWW/full.png" alt="Choropleth map" /></noscript></div> </div> </div> <style> .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper { align-items: start; display: flex; flex-direction: row; gap: 2rem; } .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper .cpm-gfx-embed { flex: 1; min-width: 18rem; } @media screen and (max-width: 30rem) { .cpm-gfx-2up-embeds-wrapper { align-items: stretch; flex-direction: column; gap: 0; } } </style> </div> </div><p></p><h3>Avances demócratas en todo Illinois</h3><p>En Chicago, el apoyo a Trump subió al 22.01% del voto de la ciudad en 2024, frente al 12.41% en 2016. En Illinois, el voto estatal de Trump creció al 45.3% en 2024, desde el 38.76% en 2016, según los resultados.</p><p>Pero la elección de noviembre dibujó un panorama de descontento nacional con las políticas de la administración de Trump, incluida la guerra en Irán, que ha impactado directamente los precios de la gasolina, así como las agresivas acciones migratorias y los problemas generales de asequibilidad que afectan a los estadounidenses.</p><p>Con victorias demócratas contundentes a favor del gobernador JB Pritzker, del fiscal general Kwame Raoul, de la contralora electa Margaret Croke y de todos los demás cargos estatales, los republicanos de Illinois se encuentran en apuros.</p><p>Los demócratas incluso avanzaron en territorios durante mucho tiempo considerados bastiones republicanos, con Ricky Rivard derrotando al representante estatal republicano de St. Charles Dan Ugaste, que cumplía cuatro mandatos.</p><p>El senador estatal por Rockford, Dave Syverson, el miembro con más tiempo en la cámara, en el cargo desde 1993, ganó por un margen estrecho frente a la demócrata Sarah Mertens, 50.8% a 49.2%.</p><p>Pritzker ganó su tercer mandato por la mayor diferencia hasta ahora, 60.6% frente al 36% de Darren Bailey. El gobernador demócrata también recuperó condados tradicionalmente rojos como Winnebago, McHenry, Sangamon y Jackson.</p><h3>El Operativo Midway Blitz, un factor motivador</h3><p>Criada en La Villita, Brenda Anaya dijo que estaba acostumbrada a ver el vecindario lleno de gente. Pero eso cambió cuando la administración de Trump lanzó el Operativo Midway Blitz el otoño pasado.</p><p>Cuando los agentes federales empezaron a llenar las calles en busca de inmigrantes indocumentados, Anaya dijo que los residentes se asustaron y dejaron de salir de sus casas.</p><p>"Mucha gente tenía miedo", dijo Anaya, de 27 años. "Fue una época difícil para todos los que vivimos aquí".</p><p>Anaya votó por los demócratas en las elecciones de medio término y estaba segura de que ganarían en Illinois. Sin embargo, se sorprendió al ver que las victorias demócratas se extendieron más allá del estado y por todo el país.</p><p>Después de que los demócratas recuperaran el control federal tanto del Senado como de la Cámara de Representantes en las elecciones de medio término, Anaya dijo que empieza a esperar que las cosas vuelvan a la normalidad.</p><p>"Cuando [los funcionarios electos] asuman el cargo, espero que hagan lo posible por detener a ICE", dijo.</p><p>Anaya espera que la aplicación de la ley migratoria se detenga no sólo en Chicago sino en todo el país.</p><p>"La gente debería sentirse segura", dijo.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>
